questions.text: What is a defining relative clause?
opts: Essential for identifying which noun is meant; no commas
Extra information about an identified noun
questions.correct: Essential for identifying which noun is meant; no commas
questions.hint: "The defining relative clause is used to identify which person or thing we mean." No commas. ✅

questions.text: Why does biographical writing use so many relative clauses?
opts: They are required by style guides
To incorporate information within a sentence rather than producing disconnected fragments
Because passive voice is too formal
questions.correct: To incorporate information within a sentence rather than producing disconnected fragments
questions.hint: "Relative clauses allow you to incorporate this information within a sentence rather than breaking it into fragments." ✅

questions.text: What is a reduced relative clause?
opts: A shorter form where the relative pronoun and auxiliary are omitted
questions.correct: A shorter form where the relative pronoun and auxiliary are omitted
questions.hint: "Reduced clauses: the relative pronoun and auxiliary are omitted." ✅

questions.text: What is the key distinction between defining and non-defining?
opts: Whether the antecedent is already identified or needs to be identified
questions.correct: Whether the antecedent is already identified or needs to be identified
questions.hint: "Whether the antecedent is already identified or needs to be identified — the fundamental principle." ✅

questions.text: Which students code-switch most naturally, according to Kamila?
opts: Those who grew up in bilingual households
questions.correct: Those who grew up in bilingual households
questions.hint: "The students WHO use the most code-switching are those who grew up in bilingual households." ✅

questions.text: What does Amir argue should be at the centre of the curriculum?
questions.correct: Communication and critical thinking skills
questions.hint: "The skills that employers consistently value are communication and critical thinking." ✅

questions.text: What is lexical borrowing, according to Dr. Asel?
opts: Borrowing technical terms that don't have equivalents in one language
questions.correct: Borrowing technical terms that don't have equivalents in one language
questions.hint: "Lexical borrowing — different from code-switching that serves a social function." ✅

questions.text: What does Zhibek argue for in the curriculum discussion?
questions.correct: Physical education and interdisciplinary learning
questions.hint: "Physical education, which is consistently undervalued..." + interdisciplinary module proposal. ✅

questions.text: What does Daniyar propose for civic education?
opts: Legal rights, institutions, and civic obligations — not parties
questions.correct: Legal rights, institutions, and civic obligations — not parties
questions.hint: "Not about political parties — about the structures through which society organises itself." ✅

questions.text: What does Kamila say about her current research model?
opts: It's complete and ready to publish
It needs to be extended — doesn't fully capture motivations
It was rejected by Dr. Asel
questions.correct: It needs to be extended — doesn't fully capture motivations
questions.hint: "The framework I've been using needs to be extended... my current model doesn't fully capture it." ✅

questions.text: What is the key thesis question Dr. Asel identifies?
opts: How many languages Kazakh students know
What are the conditions under which different types of switching occur?
questions.correct: What are the conditions under which different types of switching occur?
questions.hint: "What are the conditions UNDER WHICH different types of switching occur?" ✅

questions.text: "Any curriculum that doesn't include communication isn't preparing students" is a non-defining clause.
questions.correct: False
questions.hint: No commas + "that" = DEFINING clause. "Any curriculum THAT doesn't include..." = tells WHICH curriculum. ✅

questions.text: "The book that she wrote." — Can "that" be omitted?
opts: Yes — "she" is subject; "that" = object → can omit
questions.correct: Yes — "she" is subject; "that" = object → can omit
questions.hint: "She" follows "that" = subject position. "That" = object → can omit. "The book she wrote." ✅

questions.text: "Kamila, that studies linguistics, is brilliant." — Error:
questions.correct: "that" must be "who" — NEVER "that" in non-defining
questions.hint: ✅ "Kamila, WHO studies linguistics, is brilliant." NEVER "that" in non-defining clauses. ✅

questions.text: "The scientist ___ discovered penicillin was Fleming." (defining, people)
questions.correct: who
questions.hint: People (subject) → WHO. Defining (no commas). "The scientist WHO discovered penicillin." ✅

questions.text: "The report, which I found useful, was long." — The clause can be removed because:
opts: It's non-defining — extra info about already-identified report
questions.correct: It's non-defining — extra info about already-identified report
questions.hint: Non-defining clause = extra info. Remove it → "The report was long." Core meaning intact. ✅

questions.text: "She passed, which surprised everyone." — "which" refers to:
opts: The whole fact that she passed
questions.correct: The whole fact that she passed
questions.hint: Sentential "which" = refers to the whole preceding clause. ✅

questions.text: "The document signed yesterday" is a reduced form of:
questions.correct: "The document which was signed yesterday"
questions.hint: Passive reduction: "which was signed" → SIGNED. "The document SIGNED yesterday." ✅

questions.text: "In which" is the formal equivalent of:
questions.correct: where
questions.hint: "The room IN WHICH they met." = "The room WHERE they met." ✅

questions.text: "The year where I graduated." — Error:
questions.correct: "where" should be "when" — time noun → "when"
questions.hint: ✅ "The year WHEN I graduated." — time → WHEN, not "where." ✅

questions.text: "The sentence becomes ambiguous." "Ambiguous" means:
opts: Having more than one possible meaning; unclear
questions.correct: Having more than one possible meaning; unclear
questions.hint: "ambiguous" = having more than one possible interpretation; not clear.

questions.text: "Incorporate information within a sentence." "Incorporate" means:
opts: Include as part of a whole
questions.correct: Include as part of a whole
questions.hint: "incorporate" = to include something as part of a larger structure.

questions.text: "Whether its presence is essential or supplementary." "Supplementary" means:
questions.correct: Additional; providing extra context
questions.hint: "supplementary" = providing extra information beyond the core; additional.

questions.text: "A reduced relative clause." "Reduced" here means:
opts: Shortened by removing the pronoun and auxiliary
questions.correct: Shortened by removing the pronoun and auxiliary
questions.hint: "reduced" = made shorter by omitting the relative pronoun and auxiliary verb.

questions.text: "Makes prose feel less cluttered." "Cluttered" means:
opts: Too full of unnecessary elements; congested
questions.correct: Too full of unnecessary elements; congested
questions.hint: "cluttered" = containing too much unnecessary material; congested.
